chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadhr, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jirham, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'What do you think if a Takbirah (saying Allahu Akbar) or more missed me?' He said, 'You make up what missed you.' I said, 'Do I face the Qibla?' He said, 'Yes.' And you follow the funeral procession. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out for the funeral of a woman from the Banu al-Najjar, and he prayed over her. They found the grave (pit) but they were not enabled (to lower her in), so they placed the funeral (body) (on the ground). Whenever a group of people came, he would say to them, 'Pray over her.' (Meaning: join in the prayer).

key_terms.الْجَنَازَةَ: Al-Janazah: The funeral procession or the body of the deceased prepared for burial.
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: Al-Qibla: The direction of prayer, facing the Kaaba in Mecca.
key_terms.بَنِي النَّجَّارِ: Banu al-Najjar: A prominent clan in Medina, known for their hospitality to the Prophet.
key_terms.تَقْضِي: Qada: To make up or compensate for a missed obligatory act.
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةٌ: Takbirah: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar', a pillar of the funeral prayer.

ai.seo_question: How to make up missed Takbirat in funeral prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Tahdhib establishes the fiqh of qada (making up) missed Takbirat in Salat al-Janazah, emphasizing that the prayer remains valid even if performed individually after the main congregation. It highlights the Prophetic precedent of inclusivity, where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) invited any arriving companions to join the funeral prayer, reinforcing the communal and flexible nature of this specific act of worship.
